text: What makes two's complement worth its awkwardness compared with sign-magnitude?
choices: Subtraction becomes addition, so one adder serves for both and there is a single zero
It can represent larger numbers in the same width
It makes multiplication a single instruction
It is easier for humans to read by eye
explanation: Because values live on a circle of size 2^W, subtracting n and adding 2^W − n are the same operation — so no subtraction hardware is needed, and there is only one representation of zero. It is certainly not easier to read by eye, which is the price paid.
